subject.title: [Security] Mitigating timing attacks in GitHub Auth OAuth callback validation

question: After an owner-level authentication inventory, is there any supported GitHub OAuth callback that accepts and compares a CSRF state parameter?
rationale: The visible source contradicts the report, but the protected `security` label requires a human security owner to confirm the complete boundary before closure.

options.title: Confirm and close
options.body: Confirm device flow is the only supported GitHub authentication path and close this report as targeting nonexistent modules and behavior.

options.title: Request concrete evidence
options.body: Keep the report open temporarily and request an exact reachable endpoint, current-main call path, and reproducible timing measurements.

options.title: Route a real finding privately
options.body: If an undiscovered callback exists, move technical details to the private security channel and harden the owner plugin with the existing comparator.

recommendation.title: Confirm and close
recommendation.body: Confirm device flow is the only supported GitHub authentication path and close this report as targeting nonexistent modules and behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository security policy identifies this person as the vulnerability-report contact and the item requires a security-boundary decision.
